reports.summary: Nomura initiates Meesho coverage with a Reduce rating and DCF-based target price of INR167 (28% downside from INR233), citing significant valuation premium despite structurally sound business fundamentals. While the company benefits from secular tailwinds in India's value commerce segment and possesses an asset-light model with strong unit economics, current valuation leaves insufficient margin of safety against execution risks and intensifying competition from horizontal platforms. The analyst expects 23% NMV CAGR through FY30F with EBITDA margin expansion to 2.9%, but flags logistics disruptions and competitive pressures as key headwinds to margin improvement.
reports.connection_narrative: India's ecommerce market is experiencing a structural shift driven by three macro forces currently in play. First, digital payment infrastructure maturation through UPI adoption has scaled to 420 million users by CY26E, eliminating the friction that previously excluded rural and semi-urban consumers from online commerce. Second, demographic tailwinds from Gen Z entering the workforce are creating 50 million new digital shoppers annually with different purchasing patterns than previous generations. Third, internet penetration has deepened to 850 million users by CY26E from 430 million in CY18, fundamentally expanding the addressable market beyond metro-centric commerce. The ecommerce industry itself is now projected to grow from USD68 billion in CY24 to USD250 billion by CY30E as a percentage of total retail penetration rises from 6% to 13%. Within this landscape, Meesho occupies a unique position in the fast-growing value commerce segment targeting 250 million households in mass-market India that traditional platforms ignored. The company's asset-light model leverages its proprietary Valmo logistics platform with 18,000 partners to achieve industry-leading fulfillment costs, while AI-driven vernacular and voice-based search addresses first-time shoppers' needs. This translates to an expected 23% net merchandise value CAGR through FY30F with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding from negative 1.2% in 1QFY27 to positive 2.9% by FY30F. However, Nomura's Reduce rating reflects a crucial mismatch: Meesho currently trades at 2.0x EV/NMV on FY27 basis, a substantial premium to Eternal at 2.3x and Swiggy at 0.8x, despite both competitors exhibiting either superior growth profiles in quick commerce or cash-generative food delivery businesses. The competitive threat is intensifying, as Flipkart's May 2026 relaunch of Shopsy with gamified engagement targeting Gen Z represents a meaningful escalation, while Amazon and Flipkart are systematically building quick commerce and value commerce capabilities. The most critical catalyst to monitor over the next 12-18 months is whether Meesho can execute its advertising revenue roadmap from 3% to 5% of NMV while maintaining logistics spread expansion, as any shortfall in these high-margin revenue streams combined with competitive pricing pressure could significantly delay the path to profitability. Conversely, the primary risk is faster-than-expected user acquisition or lower-than-modeled decline in average order value from new cohorts, which would justify the current valuation multiple and necessitate multiple upside revisions.

reports.summary: Allied Blenders & Distillers is transitioning from a mass-premium whisky player to a diversified spirits company with strong premiumization momentum driven by ICONiQ White and an emerging super-premium portfolio through ABD Maestro. The company targets 26% EPS CAGR through FY29F, supported by structural margin expansion from backward integration capex of INR16bn+, achieving 48% gross margin and 18% EBITDA margin by FY28E. Initiate coverage at Buy with target price of INR850, implying 18.9% upside from current levels.
reports.connection_narrative: India's spirits market is experiencing a structural shift toward premiumization as rising incomes and changing consumer preferences drive trading up the value chain, creating substantial headroom for companies positioned in the prestige and above segments. This premiumization trend is accelerating across India's tier-2 and tier-3 cities where new legal drinkers entering the market seek aspirational brands at accessible price points, while established consumers progressively upgrade to higher-priced offerings. Simultaneously, backward integration has become critical for Indian spirits manufacturers to secure supply chains, reduce input costs, and support the production requirements of premium products like single malts that demand specific raw material quality. Allied Blenders & Distillers is ideally positioned to capitalize on these structural drivers through multiple levers. The company's flagship Officer's Choice maintains pan-India distribution with 80% penetration and strong cash generation as a mass-premium core, providing the financial foundation and logistics infrastructure to scale newer premium brands. ICONiQ White exemplifies ABDL's execution capability, becoming the world's fastest-growing millionaire whisky within three years of launch by identifying a white space at the INR500-600 price point, combining quality liquid, contemporary positioning for new-generation consumers, and aggressive geographic expansion to nine countries. The diversification through ABD Maestro into super-premium and luxury segments across whisky, gin, vodka, and rum creates multiple earnings streams and reduces dependence on a single brand, while the upcoming single malt launch in 2029 targets the ultra-premium segment with superior economics. ABDL's capex program of INR16bn+ invested across malt, ENA, and PET manufacturing directly addresses structural cost competitiveness and supply security, enabling the company to target gross margin expansion from 45.6% to 48% and EBITDA margin improvement from 13.8% to 18% by FY28E. The appointment of new management from Radico, a successful premium-focused competitor, signals strategic intent to accelerate premiumization further. The single most important catalyst to monitor is the execution trajectory of the backward integration capex across all three raw material streams, as delays or cost overruns could compress the targeted margin expansion timeline. The primary downside risk is slower-than-expected consumer adoption of premium brands or intensified competitive activity, particularly if larger multinationals like Diageo or Pernod Ricard increase focus on India's premium segments, which could pressure pricing and market share gains for ABDL.

reports.summary: This report initiates Shanti Gold with a BUY rating and target price of Rs 474 (67% upside) while upgrading Sky Gold to BUY with target price of Rs 1,068 (36% upside). Both companies are positioned to benefit from structural industry formalization as organized retail chains expand and outsource manufacturing to scaled, technology-enabled B2B producers. Shanti Gold's focused positioning in higher-margin studded jewellery combined with 4.5x capacity expansion creates compelling earnings growth visibility (39% revenue CAGR, 24% earnings CAGR FY26-29E) with superior capital efficiency metrics.
reports.connection_narrative: India's jewellery industry is undergoing a fundamental structural shift from fragmented, family-owned manufacturers toward organized, technology-enabled B2B producers. This formalization is being driven by the rapid expansion of organized retail chains seeking scalable manufacturing partners, increasing outsourcing among national retailers to improve efficiency, and growing consumer demand for designed, premium jewellery products. The organized B2B segment is capturing share as large retailers expand store networks and require consistent, design-rich inventory supplied by partners with automated manufacturing capabilities and proven execution track records. Simultaneously, premiumization trends favor higher-value categories like studded jewellery and designer pieces that command superior making charges and margins. Shanti Gold benefits from this structural opportunity by scaling manufacturing capacity 4.5x through its Marol facility ramp-up and upcoming Jaipur expansion to 7,900 kg per annum, addressing the supply constraint that currently limits its growth. The company's focused strategy on design-intensive, higher-margin products—particularly 22K cubic zirconia studded jewellery commanding 12-25% making charges—translates into gross margins of 11% versus Sky Gold's 8%, while its asset-light model and efficient inventory management generate superior ROE of 37% and ROCE of 34%. Sky Gold, meanwhile, leverages its significantly larger scale (Rs 62.9bn revenue, 14,400 kg capacity) and pan-India distribution network spanning 2,000+ retail outlets to capitalize on volume-driven lightweight daily-wear categories while steadily building export revenue now approaching 8% of sales. The company's order-linked gold procurement model limits inventory-price risk while providing downside protection. The single most important catalyst to monitor is the successful ramp-up of Shanti Gold's Jaipur expansion and the velocity of new client additions from organized retailers, which will validate the demand assumptions underpinning the 39% revenue CAGR projection. The primary risk is that slower-than-expected organized retail expansion or competitive intensity from other formatted manufacturers could pressure utilization rates and margin expansion timelines, while gold price volatility could impact working capital management despite order-linked procurement models.
